name: Prepositions of place
subtitle: Use in for rooms and spaces, on for surfaces and floors, and at for a point or a place where you do something: in the kitchen, on the wall, at the station. Next to, between, behind, in front of and opposite say exactly where things are.
source: icanspeak English original English text (grammar-a2 run, 2026-10-29)

flow.text: in · on · at · under · next to · between

concept.exampleHtml: The keys are on the table, next to the lamp. — Amira is at the station.

qa.html: in = inside a space or an area: in the kitchen, in the bag, in the car, in bed, in Leeds, in Spain. The milk is in the fridge.

on = touching a surface or a line: on the table, on the wall, on the floor, on the left. Also floors of a building and public transport: on the second floor, on the bus, on the train. But: in a car, in a taxi.
at = a point, or a place where you do something: at home, at work, at school, at the bus stop, at the door, at 10 High Street. No the in at home, at work, at school.

under (lower) · above (higher, not touching) · below (lower, not touching) · next to (at the side) · between (one thing on each side) · behind (at the back) · in front of (at the front) · opposite (on the other side, facing) · near (not far). The bank is next to the post office.
✗ I'm in home. → ✓ I'm at home. · ✗ We're in the bus. → ✓ We're on the bus. · ✗ He's in front the door. → ✓ He's in front of the door.

concept.noteHtml: With buildings, in and at are often both possible: at the station is the place where you meet, in the station is inside the building. When you move to a place, you use other words: see Prepositions of movement. For in, on, at with times, see Prepositions of time.

Meaning
Example

tables.note: Say in front of (three words) and next to (two words). Do not forget of and to.

items: at home, at work, at school (no the)
on the bus, on the train, on a plane, but in a car, in a taxi
at the station or in the station: both are possible, but at is more usual for meeting someone
on the ground floor, on the second floor
on the left, on the right
in the middle of the room
at the top / at the bottom of the stairs

listen.text: The keys are on the table, next to the lamp.
listen.note: on + a surface. next to = right beside.

listen.text: Amira is at the station. She is waiting in front of the café.
listen.note: at the station = the place. in front of = three words, always with of.

listen.text: The post office is opposite the bank, between the library and the chemist's.
listen.note: opposite = on the other side. between = one thing on each side.

exercises.title: Fill in the preposition.
exercises.hint: Think: inside, surface, point, or exactly where?

items.prompt: The picture is ___ the wall.
items.why: A picture touches the surface of the wall: on the wall.

items.prompt: My sister is ___ work today.
items.why: at work: the place where you do your job. No the.

items.prompt: The cinema is ___ the bank and the supermarket.
items.why: The bank is on one side, the supermarket on the other: between.

items.prompt: Priya lives ___ the second floor.
items.why: Floors of a building take on: on the second floor.

items.prompt: Please wait ___ the bus stop. I'll be there in five minutes.
items.why: The bus stop is a point where you meet: at the bus stop.

items.prompt: I can see the park from my window. It is ___ my house, on the other side of the road.
items.why: On the other side of the road, facing the house: opposite.

items.prompt: Kwame lives ___ Manchester.
items.why: Towns and cities take in: in Manchester.

items.prompt: The clock is ___ the door, high up on the wall.
items.why: High up, not touching the door: above.
